title: Superflow vs Usersnap
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS USERSNAP · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Usersnap is a feedback tool. Superflow is a feedback tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more waiting on a widget report to catch what a checklist could find first.
qualifier: If your agency collects site feedback through Usersnap's widget, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Usersnap hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Usersnap's AI reads feedback. It doesn't read the site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person, usually the end user, reports every issue through the widget.
Usersnap's AI sidekick categorizes, scores sentiment, summarizes, and drafts replies and hypotheses on feedback already submitted. It never scans or tests the live site.
dimensions.verdict: Usersnap's AI helps after someone reports. Superflow's agents report before anyone has to.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Anyone submits via the widget or a survey. No account or seat needed.
A formal approve or reject gate: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Usersnap's widget makes sending easy. The difference is the gate: in Superflow, the client's yes is a recorded step, not a comment.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: A widget on your live site or app, plus a browser extension, with on-page screenshot annotation.
Authenticated-site review as a named feature: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Both put feedback on the live page. Behind logins, the Usersnap side is pending verification; if it resolves even, it renders even.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Internal notes stay dashboard-only. Replies to the reporter go out by email.
dimensions.verdict: Both keep the internal debate private. Even, and it says so.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools capture proof. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Annotated screenshots and screen recordings with voice, triggered when the user submits the widget.
Auto metadata on every submission: URL, browser, device, OS, screen size.
Console and error log capture: gated to Professional and up.
dimensions.verdict: Usersnap's capture is rich once someone triggers it. Superflow's proof attaches itself, before anyone has to ask.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No memory concept in product. Nothing persists learned context across projects.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Two-way sync with Jira, Jira Product Discovery, Azure DevOps, and Linear.
dimensions.verdict: Usersnap's two-way sync is real too. The difference is which tools: Jira, Azure DevOps, and Linear there, Asana, Monday, and ClickUp here. We don't sync Jira today; if Jira is your spine, weigh that honestly.

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: free for the first 20 feedback items, then Starter $49, Growth $109, Professional $189, Premium from $369 per month billed yearly (monthly $59 / $129 / $229 / from $449). Enterprise custom.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Usersnap projects finish in Usersnap. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Usersnap's widget captures annotated screenshots and screen recordings with voice, plus auto metadata on every submission. Guests send feedback with no account. Two-way sync reaches Jira, Jira Product Discovery, Azure DevOps, and Linear. Internal notes stay private while replies go to the reporter. Surveys, a feature-request portal, and a changelog live in the same platform.
stayLine: If your goal is collecting user feedback, surveys, and feature requests through a widget, and a human reports each issue, Usersnap is a solid feedback platform. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Usersnap with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. Usersnap's AI sorts feedback a person already sent; Superflow's agents find the mistakes first. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Usersnap projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Usersnap. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We sync two-way with Jira from Usersnap.
faq.answer: Superflow syncs two-way with Asana, Monday, and ClickUp, plus webhooks and a REST API. Jira is not built in today; if Jira runs your delivery, weigh that.
